overview: James H. Rimmer, PhD is the first Lakeshore Foundation Endowed Chair in Health Promotion and Rehabilitation Sciences at the University of Alabama at Birmingham (UAB).  He is a Professor in the School of Health Professions at UAB and has an adjunct faculty appointment in the Department of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation. He is PI of the CDC-funded National Center on Health, Physical Activity and Disability. He is also the developer of a set of evidence-informed guidelines referred to as GRAIDs -- Guidelines, Recommendations, Adaptations Including Disability -- which provides researchers and program staff with an implementation science framework include people with disabilities in research and interventions.  His more recent work involves the creation of a telehealth health-to-wellness online program for people with disabilities referred to as MENTOR - mindfulness, exercise and nutrition to optimize resilience.
